Mainly because of timing and security concerns. With the election close at hand, ballots put in the mail may be delayed by the Postal Service and arrive after the state's receipt deadline, meaning they wouldn't be counted — dropping a ballot in an official drop box bypasses the mail and ensures it gets to the election office on time. Officials also note that official drop boxes are secure: they are locked, anchored, under video surveillance, and emptied by teams following chain-of-custody procedures, which guards against tampering and against the kinds of fraud claims pushed by election conspiracy theorists. Drop boxes additionally give voters a convenient, 24-hour option that reduces lines and crowding at polling places and eases the burden on election offices that are already dealing with threats and heightened security measures.
